source: the reviews of xstate: what XState does where its own tests are silent

cases.name: a root history without a target fails the initial transition

cases.name: a raised event of type '*' takes the wildcard transition
cases.test: XState's development build refuses an event of type '*' where a macrostep takes it (stateUtils.ts macrostep), and nowhere else: a raised one goes through the internal queue, which that check never sees

cases.name: a cancel of an id armed twice cancels the later timer, and the earlier fires
cases.test: system.ts scheduler: schedule keeps an earlier timeout under the same id in the clock, timerMap names the later, and any of them deletes timerMap's entry when it fires

cases.name: the earlier of two timers under one id unregisters the id when it fires, so a cancel cancels nothing
cases.test: system.ts scheduler: schedule keeps an earlier timeout under the same id in the clock, timerMap names the later, and any of them deletes timerMap's entry when it fires

cases.name: a cancel of an id a raise and then a delayed send share cancels the send, and the raise fires
cases.test: system.ts scheduler: schedule keys every delayed event by its id, whatever its target, so a delayed send and a raise under one id share timerMap's entry

cases.name: a delayed send that fires unregisters the id a later raise shares, so a cancel cancels nothing

cases.name: a forwardTo whose target is the empty string fails
cases.test: send.ts forwardTo: XState's development build throws 'Attempted to forward event to undefined actor' for any falsy target, the empty string included

cases.name: a node whose history is the empty string is atomic
cases.test: StateNode.ts reads config.history by JavaScript's truthiness: a node with no type, no children and a falsy history, the empty string or 0, is atomic, and a transition to it enters it

cases.name: a node whose history is zero is atomic
cases.test: StateNode.ts reads config.history by JavaScript's truthiness: a node with no type, no children and a falsy history, the empty string or 0, is atomic, and a transition to it enters it

cases.name: a history node whose history is the number 5 is shallow
cases.test: StateNode.ts keeps config.history as written when it is truthy and not true, and resolveHistoryDefaultTransition and getHistoryNodes treat every history but 'deep' as shallow; toJSON writes the value as the config gave it

cases.name: a history node whose history is the string "x" is shallow
cases.test: StateNode.ts keeps config.history as written when it is truthy and not true, and resolveHistoryDefaultTransition and getHistoryNodes treat every history but 'deep' as shallow; toJSON writes the value as the config gave it

cases.name: an after's delays are formatted in JavaScript's key order
cases.test: StateNode.ts getDelayedTransitions reads Object.keys(after): a delay that is an array index comes first, in numeric order, so the raises of the entry are scheduled 500 before 1000

cases.name: a parallel state's regions are entered in JavaScript's key order
cases.test: StateNode.ts builds states with mapValues over Object.keys(config.states): a key that is an array index comes first, so region '1' is entered before region 'b'

cases.name: a state's events are formatted in JavaScript's key order
cases.test: stateUtils.ts formatTransitions reads Object.keys(config.on): an event type that is an array index comes first, which the definition's transitions show

cases.name: a state value's regions are read in JavaScript's key order
cases.test: StateNode.ts getStateNodes reads Object.keys(stateValue): a region whose key is an array index comes first, so resolveState lists its nodes before those of a region written before it
